summary: On 22 March 2016 the author of left-pad and 272 other npm packages unpublished them after a naming dispute with Kik. Thousands of builds that depended on left-pad failed for about 2.5 hours until npm republished it.

overview.background: npm let authors unpublish packages without limits. left-pad was an 11-line string-padding function used widely through dependency chains.
overview.impact: Hundreds of failures per minute at around 2:30 PM Pacific, and thousands of projects broke.
overview.severity: A short but widespread build failure for about 2.5 hours.
overview.gaps: npm's account is from npm itself; the author's account is not covered.

archNote: Components and relationships come from the cited source where it describes them. Layout and labels are ours.

diagrams.title: Unpublish breaks builds that depend on it
diagrams.caption: Per npm, unrestricted unpublishing caused the disruption. npm republished left-pad 0.0.3 from a backup.

diagrams.title: Safer unpublishing and local caches (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: npm said it would make it harder to unpublish versions that other packages depend on. Builds can also cache dependencies.

afterNote: The after picture shows the corrective ideas in the source and general good practice. It is conceptual unless the source says otherwise.
timelineNote: Times are as published by the source. Entries without a clock time are given in order only.

timeline.e: Kik asks npm for the kik package name and npm decides under its dispute policy.
The author unpublishes kik and 272 other packages including left-pad.
npm sees hundreds of failures per minute.
A community member publishes a functionally identical left-pad 1.0.0.
npm announces it will republish left-pad 0.0.3.
The republishing is complete after about 2.5 hours.

rootCause.trigger: An author unpublished 273 packages after a naming dispute.
rootCause.underlying: npm allowed unrestricted unpublishing, even for packages with many dependents.
contributing: Builds fetched packages live from the registry

evidence.label: Policy statement
evidence.body: provide npm users with the package they expect
evidence.note: From npm's dispute resolution policy goal as quoted in its post.

evidence.label: A simulated build error
evidence.body: npm ERR! 404 'left-pad' is not in the npm registry.
evidence.note: Typical shape of the error; not a captured log.

fix.safety: Do not publish a different package under the same name without review. It may be malicious.

troubleshoot.scenario: A package vanished from the registry and your builds fail. Many dependencies pin an old version.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
hints: How do you get builds running?
What do you tell the team?
troubleshoot.answer: Use a mirror or cache, restore the version from backup, rerun builds and add a registry cache.

rootcause.q: How many packages did the author unpublish?

design.prompt: Design a registry that protects dependents.
design.answer: Immutable versions after a period, tombstones, dispute process and dependency alerts.

checks.q: What did npm do to fix it?
What did npm say caused the disruption?
Who published a replacement within ten minutes?
